name: Fieldstone wall section
description: A straight 1.5 m section of village fieldstone wall, 0.45 m thick and 2.4 m high: rough grey-brown blocks in staggered courses with recessed mortar, topped by a row of flat capstones. The `_low` variant is a cutaway wall (about 1.4 m) for roofless village buildings, so what is inside stays visible. The `_end` variants finish a run at a gap with a pier of big dressed quoins at the +x end. The `_rubble` variants (`_rubble`, `_rubble_2`, `_rubble_3`: three layouts, each also `_low`) are the painted look's rubble wall: irregular rounded stones of mixed sizes in rough courses, dark recessed joints, rounded cap stones about 6 cm under the plain wall's top; `_moss` adds moss cushions on the caps and at the foot of both faces. `_low_rubble_end` (also `_moss`) finishes a low rubble run at a gap with a pier of roughly dressed rubble quoins at the +x end, deeper than the wall and a little higher than its caps.

provenance.prompt: A straight section of village fieldstone wall, 1 tile long (1.5 m), about 0.45 m thick and 2.4 m high. Rough, slightly irregular grey-brown stone blocks laid in staggered courses with recessed mortar, a row of flat capstones on top. Footprint 1x1 tile; the wall runs along x through the centre of the tile, spanning the full tile width so sections join end to end. Structure, static; blocks movement and sight, cover three-quarters, not destructible. Keep the triangle count well under budget: about 25-35 blocks, few segments.
